text:
ava: Quick heads-up — I ran the offline replay on last week's production traces to tune continuous batching heuristics. Results are weird: batch sizes collapsed under the default queue policy and p95 token latency jumped. attaching logs and a short repro command.

sam: thanks for running this. can you drop the exact command + trace id?

ava: yeah: ```replay --trace s3://redwood-traces/prod/2026-03-10.json --window 600 --target-tokens 512 --queue-policy fifo --batch-formation continuous --kv-cache-enabled true --out ./replay-results/exp-512-fifo.log```

mike: what do you mean by "batch sizes collapsed"? numbers?

ava: median batch size went from ~14 -> 3 when concurrent inflight > 120k reqs in the trace window. p50 token latency stable, but p95 token latency jumped 52ms -> 88ms for generation hot-path (gpt-ish model).

jess: that sounds like the queue is shying away from waiting for more tokens. maybe the token-budget target is too low or the admission policy is rejecting large requests.

ryan: did you replay with kv-cache ON/OFF? KV cache can change per-token compute and make longer sequences more expensive causing the scheduler to favor small batches.

ava: tried both. with kv-cache disabled the batch size increased a bit (median ~7) and p95 improved to ~70ms but still worse than baseline. baseline (live traces, pre-change) was ~45ms p95.

sam: can you paste the profiler flame snippet? even a small grep of heavy ops helps.

ava: pasted below (truncated):
```
PROFILE SUMMARY (exp-512-fifo.log)
kernel_load       12.3%
attn_forward      43.1%
kv_lookup         9.7%
softmax           6.5%
dispatch_overhead 14.8%
copy/serialize    13.6%
```

mike: dispatch_overhead at 14.8% seems high. replay forced many small batches, so kernel launch overhead dominates. that matches batch size collapse.

jess: do we still have the new kernel selection heuristic from the last runtime patch? could be picking a kernel optimized for large batches that is terrible for small ones.

ava: good call — the patch added a heuristic: if median_batch_len > 10 choose kernel_v2 else kernel_v1. but our replay medians flip-flop within windows. the selector is stateful and sticky for 30s.

ryan: sticky selection + small bursts could create oscillation: selector picks v2 during a burst, then bursts end and v2 performs poorly on small batches => latency rises => admission reduces batch formation further.

sam: for the offline tuning we should simulate both sticky and stateless selectors. can you run a small A/B via replay harness: A) current sticky kernel selection B) stateless per-batch selection and compare p95/p99 and cost (GPU runtime ms)?

ava: queued. running A/B now on the same trace window, will output results to the eval harness. expecting this to finish in ~25m.

infra-bot: replay job started: job_id=rj-20260310-009, trace=s3://redwood-traces/prod/2026-03-10.json, shards=8, expected_time=28m

mike: also try a different queue policy. fifo might starve longer requests. try weighted-fair (WFQ) with token-budget target 1024 and a small headroom (10%) — see if that encourages forming medium batches.

ava: will add WFQ runs: ```replay --trace ... --queue-policy wfq --token-budget 1024 --budget-headroom 0.1```

jess: record these in the eval harness so we can do paired A/B statistics. we need p50/p95/p99, median batch size, kernel choice distribution, and GPU-ms per-token.

ryan: also capture KV cache hit ratio and cache footprint per request; some pathologies were introduced when the prefetch logic started evicting too aggressively.

ava: good note. current replay logs include kv_hit_pct and kv_cache_bytes. I saw hit_pct drop from 87% -> 62% during the bad windows.

sam: poor kv hit would explain higher attn_forward cost (more recompute). can you attach a tiny sample of the trace events around the spike? like timestamps + in_flight + median_batch_size for 1m window.

ava: pasted a short CSV from exp run:
```
ts,in_flight,median_batch_size,p95_token_ms,kv_hit
1743810000,110000,13,48,0.88
1743810060,121500,4,86,0.63
1743810120,125000,3,92,0.61
1743810180,118000,6,72,0.7
```

mike: that's convincing — big inflight bump then batch collapse and kv hit drop. looks like a feedback loop.

jess: plan: 1) run A/B stateless vs sticky kernel selector, 2) test WFQ token-budget 1024 vs current default 512, 3) replay with kv-cache eviction throttled (less aggressive), 4) run paired eval and pick config minimizing p95 while keeping GPU-ms/token low. any objections? :eyes:

ryan: +1. also add a stress run where we artificially inject many long sequences to validate worst-case.

sam: agree, and add telemetry hooks to detect oscillation in prod (median_batch_size variance over 30s > threshold) to auto-fallback to conservative selector.

ava: noted. I'll run the matrix and push artifacts to https://artifacts.redwood/ab-replay/2026-03-10/ — will ping when done.

infra-bot: replay job completed: job_id=rj-20260310-009, status=success, duration=26m12s, results_url=https://artifacts.redwood/ab-replay/2026-03-10/exp-512-fifo

jess: great. thanks ava. once we have the paired A/B stats let's convene a 15m sync to decide default policy.

ava: uploading A/B summary now (short TL;DR in artifact). initial look: stateless kernel selection improved p95 from 88ms -> 58ms on this trace; WFQ + token-budget=1024 cut p95 to 50ms but increased median GPU-ms/token by ~6%. full numbers in artifacts.

mike: that sounds like a plausible tradeoff. prefer the WFQ + stateless kernel as a default for now and add the oscillation detector Sam suggested.

sam: will write the rollback/fallback runbook once we lock config. thanks all! :thumbsup:
